text:
alex_csm: Heads-up 023: onboarding note for tenant "LuminaRetail". They have a predictable daily surge (around 5pm local) where requests spike ~15x for 2- 4 minutes. They care about user experience for checkout flows. Can we draft a short public-facing runbook + an internal ops checklist focused on caching/batching/streaming for this pattern?

leah_cs: Short, customer-friendly runbook should: 1) explain what to expect during short spikes, 2) recommend toggles (Micro-Warm), 3) give simple client SDK tips to avoid retries, 4) provide where to report issues. One page max.

diego_se: Internal checklist: enable tenant-scoped micro-warm (1 worker) during predicted windows, set batch targets to favor low latency (max_wait 25ms), and enable prefix + recent-response cache. Suggest client max_concurrency 4 and exponential backoff starting at 100ms with jitter.

nina_sre: Operational rule: automatic warm pool should be triggered when moving-average burst_ratio > 6 for 2 consecutive 60s windows. Add manual override steps and a cost estimate line for the CSM. Also include rollback: if GPU memory errors >3 within 5m after warm, shut warm pool and notify SE.

tess_pm: Important to include renewal/health signals for CSMs: escalate when any of these happen within 14 days: (a) >4 post-spike timeouts, (b) p95 latency increases by >300ms, or (c) customer reports >2 failed transactions. Map to standard "Ops Engage" play.

alex_csm: Good. Also want a brief post-burst feedback flow: automated survey 30-45 minutes after a major spike with 3 quick thumbs or numeric Qs. Link responses to renewal risk tag on account.

leah_cs: Draft survey text (customer-facing):
- Q1: "Did responses feel timely during the surge?" (Yes / No)
- Q2: "Any failed requests or errors? Please summarize." (optional free text)
- Q3: "Rate your experience 1-5."
Include simple "we might enable a warm mode" explanation.

diego_se: Pasteable internal config (for runbook):
```json
{"micro_warm":{"enabled":true,"min_vms":1,"trigger_burst_ratio":6,"trigger_window_sec":60},"batching":{"max_batch_size":6,"max_wait_ms":25},"caching":{"recent_ttl_sec":60,"prefix_ttl_sec":180},"client_reco":{"max_concurrency":4,"backoff_initial_ms":100,"jitter_pct":0.25}}
```

diego_se: Note: set recent_ttl short to avoid stale checkout state.

nina_sre: Add monitoring panel: live p50/p95, cold_starts_per_minute, warm_pool_active, burst_ratio, failed_checkouts, and survey_response_rate. Create alert: if failed_checkouts > 1% over 10m, page oncall and @alex_csm.

tess_pm: Enablement checklist for CSM before first predicted surge (10min sync): confirm customer's peak window, agree on concurrency guardrails, sanity-check sample prompts (checkout payloads), and share rollback contacts.

alex_csm: Communication snippet for customer-facing one-pager: "During brief high-traffic moments, response times may temporarily increase while we scale capacity. We recommend enabling our Micro-Warm option and following two easy client settings to keep your checkout flows smooth. We'll follow up with a short survey after big spikes to capture how things went." Keep tone reassuring and non-technical.

leah_cs: I'll produce the one-pager and attach the short survey link + expected cost delta estimate.

diego_se: I'll add the config to the internal runbook and include a small troubleshooting section: common causes for warm-pool failures and quick commands to toggle.

nina_sre: I'll wire the telemetry operator and dashboard card; will include example alert thresholds and a Canary checklist.

tess_pm: I'll update the CSM playbook with the 10-minute sync agenda and the escalation mapping to renewal risk.

alex_csm: Timeline: drafts to reviewers in 36h. Thanks team.

bot-deploy: Runbook stub created: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/cs/lumina-warmup (draft mode)
